Early board bring-up is easier to debug when each step produces a result that can be checked independently. I start by confirming the toolchain and startup flow, then verify a simple GPIO behavior before adding peripheral drivers.

title: Notes on a Repeatable Embedded Bring-Up
text:
A small, useful sequence

Build the unmodified startup project and keep the linker output available.
Program the board and confirm that the debugger can halt and inspect the expected target.
Exercise one GPIO and verify its state at the pin.
Add one peripheral at a time, checking configuration and data transfer before integrating the next component.

This sequence keeps toolchain, board, and application problems easier to separate. As project-specific test results become available, this note can be expanded with measurements, schematics, and code examples.
